'''Conference rankings''' on this wiki come from the [https://portal.core.edu.au/conf-ranks/ ICORE/CORE Conference Portal],
the most widely used ranking of computing conferences (ranks A*, A, B, C). They appear in the "Rankings" column of the
''Leading venues'' table on each topic page, next to the level from the Norwegian register.

== How the ranks are linked to OpenAlex ==
The CORE list (as kept in [https://github.com/jtapolcai/corePaperList corePaperList], <code>inputs/core_table.csv</code>)
is matched to OpenAlex sources by <code>scripts/match_core_openalex.py</code>:
# a hand-made list for conferences whose proceedings appear in OpenAlex as a journal or under another name
#: (e.g. AAAI → ''Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence'', VLDB → ''Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment'',
#: SIGMOD → ''Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data'');
# the same conference name (ignoring words such as "International", "Proceedings", "IEEE", "ACM" and years);
# the same acronym in the OpenAlex name, with at least two thirds of the significant words shared;
# nearly the same significant words.
Workshops, companion volumes and extended-abstract series do not inherit the rank of the main conference.
The latest rank is used; if the latest edition that lists the conference is older than ICORE 2026, its year is shown.

== Limitations ==
* Many papers of ranked conferences appear in OpenAlex only under a book series such as ''Lecture Notes in Computer
  Science'', which cannot be assigned to a single conference. Their rank is therefore not visible here.
* Matching by name can miss or mismatch a conference. Please report or correct errors on the talk page of this article.
* Ranks are shown for information; how they enter the evaluation criteria of a topic is decided by the experts of that topic.
